expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: [MIN-1] Swappable positional arguments... `transfer(to, from, amount)` is valid TypeScript and moves money backwards

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-1] Retrying can double-charge at [payments.ts:44]... Require an idempotency key and pass it to Stripe

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-2] Failures are silently converted to `null` at [payments.ts:55]

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-5] Money and input constraints are absent... Balances use JS `number`, which permits floating-point rounding

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-3] Raw interpolated SQL at [payments.ts:86]... `$executeRawUnsafe` embeds a runtime value in SQL

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: [MAJ-4] Subscription side effects can silently be skipped... the switch has no exhaustive/default failure

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: [CRT-1] Unsigned webhook can initiate charges... Arbitrary JSON is parsed... there is no Stripe signature verification, schema validation

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: A failure after the debit but before the credit destroys money; `transfer(to, from, amount)` moves money backwards; `"cancelled"` instead of `"canceled"` updates the DB

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Critical section: unsigned webhook, non-atomic transfers, purge defaults; Major section: retries, failures, SQL, subscription, money constraints; Minor: swappable args, receipts, config

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: [CRT-1] describes the problem but proposes no device; [CRT-3] states 'It hard-deletes without a limit or confirmation' but no concrete device; [MIN-3] notes timeout is unused with no device proposed

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
